image_description: A grey whale breaches the surface of blue ocean water, displaying its head and upper body. The whale has mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches. In the background, a kayaker is visible on the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape appears somewhat consistent with a baleen whale, but the angle and resolution make verifying the 'arched rostrum' difficult. Crucially, the two blowholes are not clearly visible or distinguishable from the general texture of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey pattern with white speckling consistent with barnacle encrustation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only shows the anterior portion (head and shoulders) of the whale. The posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be located is submerged or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and immediate shoulder area are visible. The full spindle shape cannot be verified as the rest of the body is underwater.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the visible skin exhibits the correct mottled texture and coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or obscured by water/angle; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located further back on the body and are not visible in this crop focusing on the head breach.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely out of frame/submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin surface appears rough and textured, consistent with callosities and barnacles.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The white barnacle patches appear slightly 'painted on' or overly uniform in distribution compared to the chaotic natural clustering seen in real photographs. There is a slight lack of micro-texture depth in the grey areas.

The boundary between the whale's chin and the splashing water is indistinct. The water seems to merge into the skin rather than splashing off a solid surface, suggesting a failure in fluid-solid interaction rendering.
The kayaker in the background appears disproportionately small and slightly warped, lacking clear structural definition typical of distant objects in AI generations.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the species identification beyond visual similarity, ensuring it is not a humpback or other baleen whale misclassified.
To rigorously audit the merging/splashing effect at the chin to determine if it is a physical splash or a generative artifact (melting).
To assess overall coherence, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle global artifacts missed by specific audits.
To verify if the background object is correctly identified as a kayaker/person or if it is a hallucinated structure.

focus_areas: Water displacement physics at the breach point
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the water-whale boundary. AI often fails to render crisp splashes, resulting in 'muddy' transitions. Also, verify if the barnacle patterns look procedurally generated (too uniform) vs. naturally random. The background kayaker is a strong indicator of scene coherence; if it looks like melted plastic, downgrade artifact score significantly.
